## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`Cache.set` must lower-case keys before merge: as written, any value stored under a mixed-case key can never be read back through `get`.

## Changes
This pull request adds `Cache.set`, which stores a value with an expiry of `time.monotonic() + ttl`, and raises `DEFAULT_TTL` from 60 to 300 seconds, updating the comment to match. It also adds tests for the set/get round trip, the new default TTL and expiry.

## Critical
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Lower-case the key in `Cache.set` — `c.set("Alpha", 1)` followed by `c.get("Alpha")` returns `None`, because `set` writes `self._store["Alpha"]` while `get` looks up `key.lower()` (`app/cache.py:17`). This breaks the rule at `app/cache.py:14-15` that "every path into _store lower-cases the key first". — Callers using any mixed-case key silently get cache misses, and those orphaned entries are never evicted, because only `get` deletes expired entries. — Fix: Store under `key.lower()`, and extend `test_set_then_get_round_trip` to set a mixed-case key; the current test sets `"alpha"`, so it passes against this bug.
